title: Drainage Slope Myth: Is Steeper Always Better?
description: A common myth in drainage installation is that increasing pipe slope always speeds up flow and prevents clogs. In reality, excessive slope can cause liquids to rush past solid waste, leaving solids behind to dry and build up inside the pipe. Proper drainage relies on a consistent, code-compliant slope—typically 1/4 inch per foot for standard branch lines—to maintain self-scouring velocity where liquids and solids move together. Always consult local plumbing codes for required minimum and maximum gradients based on pipe diameter.

Drainage Slope Myth: Is Steeper Always Better?

A common myth in drainage installation is that increasing pipe slope always speeds up flow and prevents clogs. In reality, excessive slope can cause liquids to rush past solid waste, leaving solids behind to dry and build up inside the pipe. Proper drainage relies on a consistent, code-compliant slope—typically 1/4 inch per foot for standard branch lines—to maintain self-scouring velocity where liquids and solids move together. Always consult local plumbing codes for required minimum and maximum gradients based on pipe diameter.
